name: Data Analyzer: An oversized dictionary upload is refused before any AI work
objective: Shows large dictionary files are stopped early so they cannot run up AI cost.
precondition: Server application loaded in the offline test harness with a made-up API key; limits are set through environment settings in each step. No network and no AI model. Dictionary and program-creation steps are replaced by stand-ins.

steps.action: Set the dictionary upload limit to 1000 bytes and upload a dictionary of about 4000 bytes.
steps.expected: HTTP 413 (too large); the error names DATA_ANALYZER_MAX_DICTIONARY_UPLOAD_BYTES; the program-creation (AI) step was never called.

name: Data Analyzer: An oversized dictionary sent without a declared size is still stopped
objective: Shows the limit cannot be dodged by omitting the size header.
precondition: Server application loaded in the offline test harness with a made-up API key; limits are set through environment settings in each step. No network and no AI model. Dictionary and program-creation steps are replaced by stand-ins.

steps.action: Set the limit to 1000 bytes and send 5000 bytes in pieces (no Content-Length header).
steps.expected: HTTP 413 and the program-creation step was never called.

name: Data Analyzer: The default dictionary size limit is 2 MB and smaller than the data limit
objective: Shows the shipped defaults: dictionaries are capped lower than data files.
precondition: Server application loaded in the offline test harness with a made-up API key; limits are set through environment settings in each step. No network and no AI model.

steps.action: Remove both limit settings and read the two default limits.
steps.expected: Dictionary limit is exactly 2,097,152 bytes (2 MB) and is smaller than the analyze limit.

name: Data Analyzer: A small dictionary upload is not blocked
precondition: Server application loaded in the offline test harness with a made-up API key; limits are set through environment settings in each step. No network and no AI model. Dictionary and program-creation steps are replaced by stand-ins.

steps.action: Set the limit to 100,000 bytes and upload a tiny dictionary.

name: Data Analyzer: A CSV with too many rows is refused with HTTP 413
objective: Shows the row cap is enforced.
precondition: Server application loaded in the offline test harness with a made-up API key; limits are set through environment settings in each step. No network and no AI model.

steps.action: Set the maximum rows to 50 and upload a CSV with 100 data rows.

name: Data Analyzer: A CSV with too many columns is refused with HTTP 413
objective: Shows the column cap is enforced.
precondition: Server application loaded in the offline test harness with a made-up API key; limits are set through environment settings in each step. No network and no AI model.

steps.action: Set the maximum columns to 5 and upload a CSV with 20 columns.

name: Data Analyzer: A CSV within the limits is still analysed
objective: Shows limits do not block normal files.
precondition: Server application loaded in the offline test harness with a made-up API key; limits are set through environment settings in each step. No network and no AI model.

steps.action: Set the maximum rows to 50 and upload a 2-row CSV.
steps.expected: HTTP 200 and the summary reports 2 rows.

name: Data Analyzer: An Excel file that expands too much is refused before it is opened
objective: Shows a 'zip bomb' style workbook (small file that is huge when unpacked) is stopped without being loaded.
precondition: Server application loaded in the offline test harness with a made-up API key; limits are set through environment settings in each step. No network and no AI model.

steps.action: Build a made-up Excel file of 3000 rows, set the unpacked-size limit to 20,000 bytes, and make the Excel-opening routine fail the test if it is reached.
steps.expected: HTTP 413; the error mentions DATA_ANALYZER_MAX_EXCEL_UNCOMPRESSED_BYTES; the Excel opener was never reached.

name: Data Analyzer: An Excel sheet with too many rows is refused before it is opened
objective: Shows the row cap is checked from the sheet's declared size without loading it.
precondition: Server application loaded in the offline test harness with a made-up API key; limits are set through environment settings in each step. No network and no AI model.

steps.action: Build an Excel file of 300 rows, set maximum rows to 100, and make the Excel opener fail the test if reached.

name: Data Analyzer: An Excel workbook with too many sheets is refused
objective: Shows the sheet-count cap is enforced.
precondition: Server application loaded in the offline test harness with a made-up API key; limits are set through environment settings in each step. No network and no AI model.

steps.action: Build a workbook with 6 sheets and set the maximum to 3.

name: Data Analyzer: A normal Excel file is still analysed
objective: Shows Excel limits do not block ordinary files.
precondition: Server application loaded in the offline test harness with a made-up API key; limits are set through environment settings in each step. No network and no AI model.

steps.action: Upload a 5-row Excel file with default limits.
steps.expected: HTTP 200 and the summary reports 5 rows.

name: Data Analyzer: A zip with too many internal parts is refused as an Excel file
objective: Shows the loader refuses an archive with an excessive number of internal files.
precondition: Data loader called directly, no server; a made-up zip is built in memory.

steps.action: Set the archive-member limit to 10 and load a zip with 30 small parts.
steps.expected: A 'data too large' error is raised.

name: Data Analyzer: The inline-data route also enforces the row limit
objective: Shows the limit applies to both ways of sending data.
precondition: Server application loaded in the offline test harness with a made-up API key; limits are set through environment settings in each step. No network and no AI model.

steps.action: Set maximum rows to 5 and send inline CSV text with 50 rows to the inline-data route.

name: Data Analyzer: A very long issue list is cut at the limit and says so, with the true total
objective: Shows the report stays a sensible size but never hides how many problems there really were.
precondition: Report-building code called directly on a made-up table; no server.

steps.action: Set the issue cap to 10 and build a report from one issue affecting 100 rows.
steps.expected: 10 issues returned; issues_returned 10; issues_total 100; issues_truncated true; summary issues_found 100 and critical_issues 100.

name: Data Analyzer: An issue list under the limit is not marked as cut
objective: Shows the truncation flag is false when nothing was cut.
precondition: Report-building code called directly on a made-up table; no server.

steps.action: Set the issue cap to 10 and build a report from one issue affecting 3 rows.
steps.expected: issues_truncated is false and issues_total equals issues_returned, both 3.

name: Data Analyzer: An analysis response includes the truncation fields
objective: Shows callers can always see the totals and truncation flag.
precondition: Server application loaded in the offline test harness with a made-up API key; limits are set through environment settings in each step. No network and no AI model.

steps.expected: HTTP 200; issues_truncated is false and issues_total equals the number of issues listed.
